summary.prose: Building s3 moves every model decision in the daemon onto the definitions in ten steps: first the settings catalog and defaults derived from the shipped file plus a build-time check, then the boot reconcile, tier resolution, the role router and provider construction through the registry, then the remaining runner literals, config.write and models.resolveRole, the TUI stopgap, and the installers and IDE settings that read the catalog. A source scan and real-daemon tests close it out.

testStrategyCoverage.lldStrategyItem: tier resolution (src/config/analyze.ts): an unset tier resolves to the fixture definitions' default with its effort; a fixture with non-empty default efforts keeps them through reconcile → parse → resolution; '' effort means the CLI default; a tier set by alias resolves to the canonical model; '' model is unset
effort: a tier whose model does not accept its effort resolves without it and logs a warning naming tier, model and effort; the built CliProvider gets no effort
decision A: an unlisted and a rejected model fall back to the tier default with a warning naming tier, requested model, reason and default

provider construction: CLI kind from registry.cliKind; Codex inputBudgetChars from the model's chars limit; haiku gets none; an Ollama tier's num_ctx is the fixture model's token limit; the summariser uses the family's summariserModel when the cheap model is not of its family

tool loop: an ollama cheap tier's model wins (today's precedence); else a listed coreModel; else registry.toolLoopModel() with a warning naming the requested coreModel; num_ctx is the chosen model's token limit
